newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Hun Sen radio says Cambodia fighting not coup.
newsitem.headline: Hun Sen radio says Cambodia fighting not coup.

text.p: A radio station controlled by Cambodia's powerful Second Prime Minister Hun Sen denied on Sunday that a coup was under way as fighting between troops loyal to the two rival prime ministers intensified in the capital.

A radio broadcast urged people to remain calm, and said government troops were fighting Khmer Rouge guerrillas in the capital. Thousands of people were fleeing the city as the fighting went into its second day.
"It is not a coup. If it were a coup FUNCINPEC ministers and officials would be arrested," the radio said, referring to First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh's royalist party.

"The government would like to appeal to the people to remain calm," the radio said. "The government is fighting with Khmer Rouge and the Khmer Rouge are shelling Phnom Penh like they did in 1975," the radio said, referring to the Maoist guerrillas' victory over a U.S.-backed government in April 1975.

Ranariddh, who is currently in France, has accused coalition partner Hun Sen of attempting a coup. Ranariddh has been negotiating with Khmer Rouge nominal leader Khieu Samphan on a legitimate political role for the rebel group.

Fighting, which started on Saturday, resumed at dawn in Phnom Penh on Sunday with shelling and small arms fire rocking the capital. The violence began on Saturday after Hun Sen ordered a crackdown against "illegal troops" being brought into the capital under Ranariddh's command.
